rule: A planned deload never falls before week 3 of a block (deloads count back every 4th week from the transition week)
summary: No trial sets a minimum number of loading weeks before a deload. Coach consensus (Bell 2023 Delphi) and athlete surveys (Rogerson 2024: deload every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks; Bell 2022 coach interviews) describe deloads as planned and/or autoregulated every few weeks, without a fixed earliest point. In trained lifters, a 1-week full training break at week 5 of 9 slightly reduced strength gains (Coleman 2024). An untrained within-subject trial found reduced-volume deloads did not hurt hypertrophy (Pancar 2026). Together this argues against deloading too early and too often, and earliest_week 3 (at least 2 loading weeks, with the previous transition week counting as a deload-like week 0) is a reasonable floor. The number itself is untested.

sources.note: Bell 2023 Delphi (21 coaches in final round): consensus definition of deloading as reduced stress to manage fatigue; design principles, no evidence-based timing
Rogerson 2024 survey (n=246 strength/physique athletes): deload ~6.4 days every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks, planned or combined with autoregulation
Bell 2022 interviews with 18 coaches: deloading is a periodic, intentional cut in training demand; practice varies
Coleman 2024, trained adults: a 1-wk full break mid-programme gave less strength gain and equal hypertrophy, which argues against unnecessary early or complete deloads
